newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Aid agencies unite in appeal over Zaire conflict.
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies unite in appeal over Zaire conflict.

text.p: The leaders of the world's four biggest humanitarian organisations launched an unprecedented joint appeal on Friday for help for thousands of refugees trapped by fighting in eastern Zaire.

Sadako Ogata, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, Carol Bellamy, executive director of UNICEF, Catherine Bertini, executive director of the World Food Programme and Emma Bonino, European Union Commissioner responsible for humanitarian affairs, said urgent help was needed.
"We appeal to the participants...to fully consider the urgent humanitarian needs of hundreds of thousands of refugees and displaced Zaireans stranded in the war zone," they said in a statement.
The appeal was timed to coincide with talks in South Africa between Zairean government officials and members of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire.
Bonino also issued a separate appeal with Xavier Emmanuelli and Reginald Moreels, respectively French and Belgian junior ministers entrusted with humanitarian aid to Africa.
That appeal, released by Emmanuelli's office in Paris, said thousands of people were threatened with death by starvation.
The rebels have overrun a huge swathe of eastern Zaire since October last year, scattering thousands of Rwandan refugees and Zairean peasant farmers who lived in the area.

The crisis has been exacerbated by the prolonged absences of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, whose 31-year grip on the central African country was loosened by his frequent visits to Europe for treatment for prostate cancer.
Mobutu appointed opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi as prime minister this week, but rebel leader Laurent Kabila rejected an offer of six key posts in the new government.
The statement from the four aid organisations said relief workers urgently needed access to areas from where reports of thousands of starving refugees were emerging.

"We have witnessed the plight of the refugees ourselves. These people fled into the rain forest to escape the fighting and violence in the region. We are now trying to help them and prepare them for repatriation," it said.
"However, many thousands of Rwandan and Burundi refugees as well as internally displaced Zaireans remain out of reach. We are appealing to the international community for urgent assistance."
